🍁The Sunday Spotlight🍁

Your Ballot, Besides the Governor
Early voting opens Saturday. The governor's race gets the headlines; here is everything else our three towns will see, from the statewide offices down to the town. Congress and the governor are in The Ballot, further down. No endorsements. An AI wrote this section.
1. On every ballot in the state. Attorney General: Democrat Letitia James, the incumbent, against Republican Saritha Komatireddy. Comptroller: Democrat Thomas DiNapoli, the incumbent, against Republican Joseph Hernandez. What the jobs are: the attorney general is the state's lawyer, who sues companies, defends state laws in court and handles consumer complaints; the comptroller is the state's auditor, who checks how money is spent and manages the state workers' pension fund. What to know: both incumbents are running again, so a vote here is mostly a vote on how they have done the job.
2. The judges (North Tonawanda and Dunkirk). State Supreme Court, 8th District, which includes Erie, Niagara and Chautauqua counties: you vote for four of seven candidates. In New York, "Supreme Court" is the main trial court for big civil cases, such as major lawsuits and divorces, not the state's highest court. Two candidates, Amodeo and Richardson, are endorsed by both parties, so the real contest is for the other two seats: Democrats Bucki and Joynt against Republicans Tripi and Hickey, with Vario on the Conservative line. What it means for you: judges rarely campaign hard, so this is the part of the ballot most people skip. The justices serve 14-year terms. Scottsville is in a different judicial district.
3. North Tonawanda. State Senate, 62nd District: Republican Rob Ortt, the incumbent and the Senate's Republican leader, against Democrat Thomas Arida. State Assembly: the city is split. Part is in the 140th, where Democrat William Conrad, the incumbent, faces Republican challenger Faisal; part is in the open 145th, Republican Becky Wydysh against Democrat Nate McMurray, who ran for Congress in 2018 and 2020. County Legislature: in Districts 7, 8 and 9, Republicans Gooch, Andres and Bradt face Democrats Mooradian, Kennedy and Osborn. The yes-or-no question: whether the city should borrow up to $18 million for a community center at the Keller Building to replace the old youth and senior centers. It would be paid with a special property tax of about 84 cents per $1,000 of assessed value before any grants; on a house assessed at $150,000, that is about $126 a year, and grants would bring it down. Early voting: Wheatfield Community Center, 2790 Church Rd, or Wendelville Fire Co., 7340 Campbell Blvd, Oct 24–Nov 1.
4. Dunkirk. State Senate, 57th District: Republican George Borrello, the incumbent, against Democrat Victoria Guite-Williams. Assembly, 150th District: Republican Andy Molitor, the incumbent, against Democrat Carle. County: Legislature District 1, Democrat Buchanan, the incumbent, against Republican Garza; District 2, Democrat Bankoski unopposed. Family Court judge: Republican Sullivan, the incumbent, against Democrat Moss. Sheriff Quattrone, a Republican, is unopposed. No ballot questions. Early voting: the County Fairgrounds 4-H Building, 1089 Central Ave, Oct 24–Nov 1.
5. Scottsville. State Senate, 54th District: Republican Pam Helming, the incumbent, against Democrat Mills. Assembly, 139th District: Republican Steve Hawley, the incumbent, against Democrat Wolcott. District Attorney Green, a Democrat, and Wheatland Supervisor Kirch, a Republican, are unopposed. No ballot questions. Early voting: the nearest sites are Henrietta Library, 625 Calkins Rd, and Gates Presbyterian, 1049 Wegman Rd; any of the county's 15 sites works, Oct 24–Nov 1.
Coming down the road. Saturday, Oct 24, is both the first day of early voting and the last day to register; early voting runs through Nov 1, and polls are open 6 a.m. to 9 p.m. on Election Day, Nov 3. Every county board of elections posts a sample ballot online; look yours up before you go so nothing on the back side surprises you. The race-by-race tracker is at benthambulletin.github.io/election.

✶The Ledger✶

Volunteer firefighter tax credit
$800
Governor Hochul signed a law raising the state tax credit for volunteer firefighters and ambulance workers to $800 a year, from $200; married couples who both serve get $1,600.

✶The National Wire✶

1

Truck Hits a Kids' Soccer Game

A pickup drove onto a field during a children's soccer game at Wichita's Stryker Soccer Complex Saturday, killing a 6-year-old boy and a 35-year-old man. Police are investigating.

2

Deadly Fire at a Canadian Base

Several people were killed or hurt in a major fire at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright in Alberta. Officials have not given a cause or a death toll, calling the situation "very active and delicate."

3

Riots in Paris

More than 1,800 people were arrested across France as protests turned violent, with looting and burned buildings. Police used tear gas on masked crowds throwing fireworks in the Place de la République.

4

Trump Lifts Russia Sanctions

The president temporarily ended many of the restrictions on Russia that Congress recently passed, citing national security. Ukraine's President Zelensky said the decision "seems wrong."

☑The Ballot☑

Sixteen Days Out
Governor. Kathy Hochul leads Bruce Blakeman by 11 to 12 points in the two most recent major polls, Marist (53 to 42, Oct 1–4) and Emerson (52 to 40, Oct 3–5); Siena had it at 9 in September. Blakeman leads upstate, where all three of our towns are. One small text-message poll last week had it at 3, against every major poll. In their only debate last Tuesday night they sparred over energy costs, immigration and public safety. What it means: Hochul is still the clear favorite; no new statewide poll came out this week.
NY-26, North Tonawanda. Democrat Tim Kennedy, the incumbent, against Republican Dennis Hannon. The Cook Political Report rates it solidly Democratic; Kennedy won 65 percent in 2024.
NY-23, Dunkirk. Republican Nick Langworthy, the incumbent, against Democrat Aaron Gies. No public poll; the district leans Republican.
NY-25, Scottsville. Democrat Joe Morelle, the incumbent, against Republican McIntyre. No public poll; the district leans Democratic.
The state's one close House race is in the Hudson Valley: Republican Mike Lawler against Democrat Cait Conley in NY-17, 48 to 46 for Conley in the one independent poll, which Cook calls a toss-up.
The national read. Democrats lead the generic ballot, the question of which party you'd vote for in your House race, by about 8 to 9 points in the averages, and Cook moved 11 more House races toward them on Friday. The Senate is close to a coin flip: Democrats need a net gain of four seats, holding Michigan and Minnesota and winning four of six Republican-held races that are within the polls' margin of error. Betting markets give them a little better than 6 in 10. The president's approval is about 21 points underwater.
Early voting Oct 24–Nov 1 · register by Oct 24 · Election Day Nov 3, 6 a.m.–9 p.m. · every race: benthambulletin.github.io/election

⛪The Home Wire⛪

1

Rochester · Bills on the Bricks

Football on the Bricks, the city's longest-running free concert series, hosts a Bills watch party at the Rochester Public Market today. Doors open at 1 p.m., with the band BBDANG at 1:30 before the 4:25 kickoff.

2

Dunkirk · A Gold Medal Graduate

Riley Grey Smith Mallon, a 2025 Dunkirk High School graduate, has earned the Congressional Award Gold Medal. He is now a sophomore at the Rochester Institute of Technology.

3

Fredonia · Ability Awareness Awards

The Resource Center holds its 37th Ability Awareness Awards on Tuesday, Nov. 3, at the White Inn in Fredonia. The luncheon honors the achievements of people with disabilities and those who support them.

★The Marquee★

1

Tarantino's Last Film Is Written

Quentin Tarantino confirmed he has finished the script for his tenth and, he has long said, final film. He won't start on it yet; he says he wants to "live a little" first.

2

Iron Maiden's Last Leg

The metal band announced its 2027 Run for Your Lives North American tour, starting in April. It is the third and final leg of the band's 50th-anniversary run.

3

Stars at the Academy Museum Gala

Taylor Swift, Sabrina Carpenter and Jennifer Hudson were among the stars on the carpet at the Academy Museum's annual gala in Los Angeles. Colman Domingo, Rami Malek and Jamie Lee Curtis were there too.
